_comment: The demo market. This file is the ONLY thing the demo supplies.
Everything a person sees in the buyer UI when `devstack/run.py` is running comes out of a
real HTTP response from a real service on a real loopback socket. This file supplies the
merchant side of that world and nothing else: three stores' approved envelopes, their
catalogues, their live stock, the platform's trust reading of each of them, and the two
conversations a reader can type in to reach them. No shortlist, no ranking, no price, no
verdict and no permalink is written down here - every one of those is computed by the real
store agents, the real exchange and the real buyer service at run time.
WHY THE CLUSTER IDS ARE PINNED. `buyer_svc.intent.clarifier._cluster_id` is a sha256 over
(query.casefold(), budget_band, hard_constraints, preferences) truncated to 16 hex and
prefixed `cl-`. A store agent declines a solicitation whose cluster is not in its envelope's
`pursue_clusters` (DeclineReason.cluster_not_pursued), so these strings have to match the
clarifier's answer byte-for-byte or the demo shows three declines. They were measured by
running `clarify(turns)` on this tree, not guessed:
clarify(['looking for a winter hat', '$80'])                              -> cl-4b6a37aebc537bd5
clarify(['I want a warm merino wool beanie for winter, under $100'])      -> cl-4d3c3e4edadaa5e7
The exact turn wording matters, and that is measured too rather than assumed: the same
opener answered with 'my budget is about $80' instead of '$80' clarifies to a DIFFERENT
cluster (cl-d401b1642abedc5e, and no hard constraint at all), which no envelope here
pursues. That is not a bug in the demo - it is the clarifier reading a hedged answer as an
unresolved constraint - but it is why `conversations[].turns` are written out verbatim.
The `intent` recorded on each conversation is the clarifier's own measured answer for those
turns, with two fields replaced by fixed values: `intent_id` (unique per session by design)
and `created_at` (the wall clock). Neither participates in the cluster hash, so replacing
them cannot change which stores are reached. They are here so a probe can drive
`POST /auctions` directly with the same intent the UI produces; the UI itself never reads
them - it calls `POST /buyer/intent/clarify` and uses what comes back.

conversations.title: A winter hat under $80
reaches: demo-woolworks bids (beanie-merino-01 at 78.00 satisfies price_usd lte 80)
demo-alpine-supply bids (beanie-merino-pro at 72.00 satisfies it too)
demo-fastfleece bids (beanie-fleece-01 at 45.00 satisfies it) and is then EXCLUDED by
the exchange's ranking because the trust snapshot blacklists it - a real R12 exclusion
carrying a real reason string, which is the point of having it in the market at all

conversations.title: A merino wool beanie under $100
reaches: demo-fastfleece DECLINES at the store agent with HTTP 204 and
x-proxyshop-decline-reason: no_matching_product - its only product is fleece. The
exchange turns that non-200 into an entry with fallback: true,
fallback_reason: 'no_response'. A second real refusal, from a different layer.
turns: I want a warm merino wool beanie for winter, under $100

intent.query: I want a warm merino wool beanie for winter, under $100

_comment: The blacklisted store, and it is here on purpose. Its eligibility word is 'eligible'
so the exchange's R12 gate does NOT deny it up front - it is solicited, it really
bids, and it is then thrown out by the ranking's blacklist filter reading the trust
snapshot below. That path is the one worth showing: the buyer UI's diagnostics get a
real `excluded[]` row carrying a real reason string produced by
`exchange.ranking.filters.blacklist_reason`, rather than a store that was quietly
never asked. Change `eligibility` to 'blacklisted' and it lands in `denied[]` instead,
which is a different (also real) story.
It is also the cheapest offer in the market at 45.00, so if it ever reaches a shortlist
slot the trust exclusion has stopped working and the demo says so loudly by showing it.
